tasks.short: Check the safety sheet and risk assessment, work with protection in the safety cabinet, decontaminate and dispose of waste, log use of toxic substances and report incidents.

steps.what: Medical scientist checks the safety data sheet and risk assessment before work
Medical scientist follows strict safety procedures when handling toxic materials in the safety cabinet
Medical scientist decontaminates surfaces and disposes of waste to avoid contamination
Medical scientist logs use of toxic substances in the register
Medical scientist reports incidents and near misses

tasks.design: The electronic lab notebook ({OTHER}) links each substance in a protocol to its safety data sheet and the lab's risk assessment, so they open with the protocol. Scanning a container in the inventory system logs the amount used to the substance register, and a short incident form replaces paper. Handling, decontaminating and disposing stay with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety sheets were in folders and the register was kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Lab notebooks link safety sheets, and inventory systems log use by scan.
tasks.still_hard: Safe work depends on habits at the bench, not records.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a cracked tube before it is opened.

reach.learn: Whether scanned use makes the register complete.

evidence.claim: Lab notebooks link safety data sheets to protocols, and inventory systems log use by barcode scan.
Audit trails that log who did what may count as a facility able to observe performance, needing works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the protocol to incident reports; waste collection is outside.
Input contract: safety sheets from suppliers; risk assessments by the lab safety officer; fallback is paper folders.
Handling and decontaminating do not change.
research_questions: Is the register complete at audit?

incremental.description: Medical scientist scans containers at use.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is careful bench work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design the exposure experiment, run the assays, move instrument output into the analysis, compute dose-response curves, evaluate the effects and write the results section.

steps.what: Medical scientist designs the exposure experiment
Medical scientist runs the assays with drugs, pesticides or microorganisms
Medical scientist copies plate reader output into spreadsheets
Medical scientist calculates dose-response curves and statistics
Medical scientist evaluates the effects at various levels
Medical scientist writes the results section with figures

tasks.design: Instruments write their output to the lab notebook ({OTHER}) with the plate layout, and a versioned analysis script, tested on reference data sets, computes dose-response curves, statistics and figures. Designing, running assays and evaluating the effects stay with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Output was copied into spreadsheets and curves fitted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Instruments export to lab notebooks, and versioned analysis pipelines are common.
tasks.still_hard: Odd plates and outliers need the scientist's judgement before analysis.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that an effect is an artefact of the solvent, not the drug.

reach.learn: Whether direct export cuts transcription errors.

evidence.claim: nf-core offers community bioinformatics pipelines with tagged releases, containers and tests.
Audit trails in lab systems may count as a facility able to observe performance.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the results section; publication is outside.
Input contract: plate layouts set by the scientist; analysis scripts kept by the lab's data analyst; fallback is spreadsheets.
Designing, running and evaluating do not change.
Scripts are tested on reference data before each version.

incremental.description: Medical scientist checks script output on each new assay type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: New assay types need script work first.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Screen the literature, write the study protocol, prepare ethics and permit applications, direct the team and follow recruitment and data completeness.

steps.what: Medical scientist screens the literature to frame the study

loop.input: Titles and abstracts from saved database searches and the study's inclusion criteria.
loop.output: Include or exclude per abstract with the criterion it rests on.
loop.check: Every cited record must resolve to a DOI or database ID; a second scientist checks a random sample of excluded abstracts.
loop.stop: One pass per search; uncertain abstracts go to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters miss relevant studies and pass many irrelevant ones.

steps.what: Medical scientist plans studies to investigate disease and treatments in a protocol
Medical scientist fills in ethics and permit applications
Medical scientist directs the study team and reviews progress
Medical scientist tracks recruitment and data completeness in spreadsheets

tasks.design: A bounded screening step sorts abstracts from saved searches by the inclusion criteria and cites the criterion; the scientist reads includes and uncertain items, and a colleague checks a sample of excludes. Ethics and permit forms fill from the protocol's sections. Recruitment and data completeness come from the study's data capture system ({OTHER}) as a dashboard. Writing the protocol and directing the team stay with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Screening was done abstract by abstract, forms written from scratch and progress tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models screen abstracts against criteria, and data capture systems report progress.
tasks.still_hard: Generated citations can be invented; every record must resolve to a real ID.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the study question that will actually change treatment.
tasks.altitude: The scientist checks screened lists instead of reading every abstract.

evidence.claim: otto-SR redid 12 Cochrane reviews (146,276 citations) in about two days, with screening sensitivity 96.7% against 81.7% for dual human review (preprint abstract).
GPT-3.5 fabricated 55% and GPT-4 18% of 636 generated citations.
Research use of health data needs safeguards under GDPR article 89.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research idea to study progress; analysis and publication are outside.
Input contract: saved searches set by the scientist with the library; form templates from the ethics committee; fallback is reading every abstract.
Protocol writing and directing do not change.
A colleague checks a sample of excluded abstracts.
research_questions: How many relevant studies does the screening miss here?

already_counted.description: Medical scientist reads includes and uncertain abstracts.
Medical scientist checks the filled applications.

incremental.description: A colleague checks a sample of excluded abstracts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Protocol writing and directing are most of this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare tissue and cell samples, examine them under the microscope, label and register samples, file microscope images and write findings.

steps.what: Medical scientist prepares organ, tissue and cell samples
Medical scientist examines samples to identify toxicity, bacteria or cell structure
Medical scientist labels samples by hand and records them in the sample list
Medical scientist saves and names microscope images by sample
Medical scientist writes findings in the lab notebook

tasks.design: The sample system ({OTHER}) prints barcode labels at receipt and logs each sample, and the microscope software saves images under the scanned sample barcode. A notebook template per assay type links findings to samples and images. Preparing and examining samples stay with the scientist; no AI reads the slides.
tasks.previous_blocker: Labels were handwritten, images renamed by hand and findings written in paper notebooks.
tasks.enabler_now: Sample systems print barcodes, and microscope software links images to sample IDs.
tasks.still_hard: Samples from outside arrive with handwritten labels.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting an unusual cell shape no protocol mentions.

evidence.claim: Sample systems print barcode labels and log samples, and microscope software links images to sample IDs.
Human tissue and cell samples carry health data, a special category under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from received samples to the notebook entry; reporting results is outside.
Input contract: samples from clinics and partner labs; label format set by the lab manager; fallback is handwriting.
Preparing and examining do not change.

incremental.description: Medical scientist relabels outside samples on receipt.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is bench and microscope work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The medical scientist keeps study design, bench work and judgement; copying output, screening every abstract and handwritten labels shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A scientist who spends saved hours on the next experiment.
